target identity\\012* Later stages guessing what the game should become\\012* Focal identity omitted or too generic\\012\\012#### remix_v5.analysis.mechanics_taxonomy_and_semantic_tags — Produce mechanics ranking, classification, and semantic tags\\012\\012**Intent:** Preserve the requirement to describe the intended remixed game in structured taxonomy outputs, not just prose.\\012\\012**Required actions:**\\012\\012* Rank the top gameplay-mechanics matches for the intended remixed game rather than the raw source game alone.\\012* Write a companion classification artifact with scores, reasoning, inheritance notes, and uncertainty.\\012* Generate semantic tags spanning theme, setting, characters, focal identity, mechanics, mood, similar games, and preserve/transform identity.\\012* Include tags for authored-world identity and procedural motif language when applicable.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* mechanics ranking file\\012* companion classification file\\012* semantic tags file\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* The remixed game is described in both human-readable and machine-readable forms.\\012* Later systems can classify or search the result without reverse-engineering prose.\\012* Tags distinguish mechanic similarity from presentation transformation.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Losing taxonomy outputs during prompt simplification\\012* Only having a narrative description with no structured tags\\012* Ranking mechanics for the wrong game target\\012* Search/classification metadata that hides the actual remix identity\\012\\012#### remix_v5.analysis.progression_core_and_five_level_plan — Define the 1.5-level core and five-level progression\\012\\012**Intent:** Force explicit progression planning even when the source game lacks explicit levels.\\012\\012**Required actions:**\\012\\012* Define the smallest practical progression proof: Level 1 and Level 1.5.\\012* Plan five levels of difficulty intent and five levels of visual evolution.\\012* Specify safe knobs, protected mechanics, hazard/reward interpretation, HUD messaging, and visual beats for each level.\\012* Make each stage feel like a related evolution of the same world, not random decorative variation.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* one_point_five_level_core\\012* five_level_difficulty_progression\\012* five_level_visual_evolution\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* Progression semantics are defined even if explicit level files never exist.\\012* World and visual phases can execute progression without guessing.\\012* Escalation supports learning, pressure, and authored-world evolution.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Flat remixes with no escalation logic\\012* Late-stage guessing about level progression\\012* Visual evolution detached from difficulty planning\\012* Progression reduced to arbitrary color changes\\012\\012#### Subgroup `progressive_disclosure_reasoning` — Progressive Disclosure Reasoning\\012\\012#### remix_v5.analysis.progressive_disclosure_and_complexity_rationale — Preserve progressive-disclosure planning value\\012\\012**Intent:** Preserve high-value progression reasoning without forcing separate level-file generation by default.\\012\\012**Use when:**\\012\\012* Whenever the remix needs explicit progression reasoning, even if it does not emit separate level HTML files.\\012\\012**Required actions:**\\012\\012* Explain what the player is learning, what is withheld, and what pressure is added across the intended progression curve.\\012* Separate real difficulty dimensions from fake difficulty and clutter.\\012* Document why the escalation model fits this specific game.\\012* Tie progression to world semantics, feedback intensity, and scene evolution when safe.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* mechanics_complexity_decomposition.md\\012* progressive_disclosure_plan.md\\012* level_adapter_rationale.md\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* Progression is explainable as a learning and pressure curve rather than arbitrary tuning.\\012* World and visual evolution can hang on a reasoned escalation model.\\012* Presentation becomes richer without confusing the player.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Losing progressive-disclosure planning value\\012* Escalation that is only numeric or decorative\\012* No rationale for why progression fits the game\\012* Confusing players with ornamental difficulty\\012\\012#### Subgroup `analysis_artifacts_and_handoff` — Analysis Artifacts and Handoff\\012\\012#### remix_v5.analysis.procedural_art_system_and_downstream_contract — Plan the procedural art system and downstream contract\\012\\012**Intent:** Give later phases a reusable visual language plus explicit obligations.\\012\\012**Required actions:**\\012\\012* Define motif vocabulary, focal silhouette, icon style, background layers, animation principles, entity families, and implementation preferences.\\012* Write a downstream contract for world, visual, and QA execution.\\012* Prefer structured `remix_plan_v4.json`-style outputs when feasible for compatibility with existing runners.\\012* Identify which old visuals should be replaced, demoted, or only used as fallback evidence.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* procedural_art_system\\012* downstream_stage_contract\\012* remix_plan_v4.json\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* Later phases know what to preserve, draw, refine, and verify.\\012* The procedural identity is specific enough to drive visuals and QA.\\012* The handoff creates a path toward an authored scene rather than generic gradients.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Visual style invented too late\\012* No explicit phase handoff\\012* Procedural art reduced to generic gradients\\012* Focal identity left until final polish\\012\\012## Phase 2 — Direct Rebuild Phase\\012\\012This phase is the regeneration spine of the workflow. Phase 1 prepares it. Phases 3–5 enrich, realize, and prove it.\\012\\012The direct rebuild phase owns `_old` preservation, canonical new `index.html` creation, blueprint-first regeneration, subsystem-by-subsystem mechanic verification, and stability-first runtime selection.\\012\\012Use `3d gta game` here to steer how the regenerated public surface expresses mechanic meaning, authored presentation, focal identity, and stable target identity without collapsing into legacy imitation.\\012\\012The new canonical surface should not feel like a decorated copy of the old public entrypoint. It should be a stable, mechanic-faithful, public-facing regeneration that is free to rebuild presentation, UI, scene structure, and visual language wherever those surfaces are not mechanic-critical.\\012\\012### Prime Directive\\012\\012Build a new, stable, original game surface while preserving mechanic truth.\\012\\012Your output should be:\\012\\012* more original than the old source\\012* mechanically grounded in the upstream blueprint\\012* stability-first in architecture and implementation choices\\012* explicitly checked against preserved legacy references before risky rewrites land\\012* visually and semantically transformed enough to feel like a fresh public game experience\\012\\012Mechanic fidelity is mandatory. Old presentation fidelity is not mandatory unless a presentation detail is truly required for gameplay comprehension or control safety.\\012\\012### Inputs You Must Treat As Authoritative\\012\\012Use the Phase 1 outputs first:\\012\\012* mechanic decomposition\\012* protected mechanics\\012* safe theming surfaces\\012* complexity profile\\012* remix premise\\012* focal identity plan when present\\012* 1.5-level core definition\\012* five-level progression intent\\012* procedural visual identity\\012* any `remix_plan_v4.json` or equivalent planning artifact required by the current runner\\012\\012The blueprint and mechanic analysis are the main source of truth for this step.\\012\\012The old runtime is evidence, not a creative prison.\\012\\012### Hard Delivery Constraint — Single Rebuilt Public Surface\\012\\012The new game must be delivered primarily through a **single rebuilt public `index.html`**.\\012\\012Required:\\012\\012* the new public `index.html` is the canonical rebuilt surface\\012* all newly authored application code should be written inline in that same `index.html` whenever feasible\\012* inline CSS in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* inline JavaScript in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* prefer a self-contained rebuilt surface over a scattered new file graph\\012* prefer a fresh, coherent runtime surface over patched legacy presentation\\012\\012Allowed exceptions only when truly justified by stability:\\012\\012* existing local assets already required by the source game\\012* media selected from approved catalogs\\012* carefully chosen external OSS CDN libraries when they materially improve stability or execution quality\\012\\012If you use an external library, justify it briefly in your planning notes before implementation.\\012\\012### Engine / Library Selection Rule\\012\\012Before implementation, choose the most stable practical runtime approach for the job.\\012\\012Examples that may be appropriate depending on the game:\\012\\012* plain JavaScript + DOM/CSS\\012* Canvas + plain JavaScript\\012* Phaser from a stable CDN\\012* jQuery for light DOM/state glue\\012* a small combination of the above when justified\\012\\012Selection criteria in order:\\012\\0121. stability\\0122. mechanic fidelity\\0123. implementation clarity\\0124. ease of testing and repair\\0125. mobile readability and input safety\\0126. originality/expressiveness\\012\\012Do not choose a heavier engine or library just because it is fashionable.\\012\\012Use the simplest browser-native path that can produce a vivid authored result.\\012\\012### Approved Media / Library Sources\\012\\012You may use:\\012\\012* approved local audio catalogs\\012* approved local GIF/media catalogs\\012* popular open-source CDN libraries when stability and maintainability benefit\\012\\012Do not introduce random, obscure, fragile, or poorly supported dependencies.\\012\\012If stability is in doubt, prefer simpler technology.\\012\\012If visual richness can be achieved with CSS, SVG, Canvas, DOM composition, or small inline helpers, prefer that over asset-heavy substitution.\\012\\012### Mission\\012\\012Using the upstream blueprint:\\012\\0121. preserve the old runnable source under `_old` names\\0122. create a new public implementation surface\\0123. begin building an entirely new game from the blueprint/mechanics analysis\\0124. keep the `_old` files as reference-only fallback material\\0125. make the new canonical surface visibly authored, coherent, and prompt-driven\\012\\012### Mandatory Pre-Build Planning Pass\\012\\012Before you start creating the new public `index.html`, first produce a short implementation plan in the workspace describing how the blueprint and known mechanics interact with the old reference.\\012\\012That plan must:\\012\\012* cite relevant old code pieces when identifiable\\012* name the mechanic surfaces that matter most\\012* explain how the blueprint maps onto those mechanic surfaces\\012* identify what is fragile\\012* identify what is easy to update safely\\012* identify what should not be touched conceptually\\012* identify which old presentation surfaces are safe to replace or demote\\012* identify how the focal identity and authored world will appear in the new canonical surface\\012* note where `_old` reference checks are required before rewriting\\012\\012At minimum, the plan should comment on:\\012\\012* player input/control handling\\012* movement/update loop\\012* collision/hit detection\\012* scoring/progression signals\\012* fail/win state handling\\012* UI/HUD surfaces\\012* focal actor/entity representation\\012* background/scene ownership\\012* media/asset wiring\\012\\012This planning pass should exist before the main rebuild work proceeds.\\012\\012### Required Sequence\\012\\012#### A. Preserve old runtime surfaces\\012\\0121. Find the current public entrypoint, especially `index.html`.\\0122. Rename it to an `_old` form.\\012\\012   * Prefer `index_old.html`.\\0123. Inspect that preserved HTML and rename directly linked **local** CSS/JS files into `_old` forms too.\\012\\012   * Prefer `styles_old.css`, `game_old.js`, etc.\\0124. Update the preserved HTML so it still resolves correctly against the renamed `_old` assets.\\012\\012#### B. Establish the new public surface\\012\\0125. Create or overwrite a fresh public `index.html` as the new canonical implementation surface.\\0126. Start building the new game from the upstream blueprint rather than patching the old source in place.\\0127. Prefer newly authored structure, UI, art systems, scene construction, and code paths when safe.\\0128. Keep the rebuilt implementation inline in the same new `index.html` unless a clearly justified stability reason prevents it.\\0129. Make the new public surface feel like the real finished game, not a wrapper around legacy structure.\\012\\012#### C. Reference-only old surfaces\\012\\01210. Treat `_old` files as evidence/reference only.\\01211. Inspect them only when:\\012\\012* mechanic behavior is ambiguous\\012* edge-case expectations are unclear\\012* you need to avoid accidental mechanic drift\\012* you need to confirm that a presentation change will not break a real gameplay expectation\\012\\012#### D. Component-by-component verification during rewrite\\012\\01212. For each rewritten component or mechanic-facing subsystem, compare it against the old reference before finalizing.\\012\\012This includes, where relevant:\\012\\012* control/input behavior\\012* animation/update timing\\012* collision/contact behavior\\012* score/progress reporting\\012* fail/win transitions\\012* HUD feedback\\012* mobile tap/click paths\\012* gameplay-critical visibility\\012\\012If a rewritten component is more original but less stable, less testable, or mechanically less truthful, revise it.\\012\\012If a rewritten component is mechanically safe but visually generic, under-authored, or too similar to the old surface, strengthen the presentation before final handoff.\\012\\012### Rules\\012\\012* Do not let `_old` files remain the main implementation surface.\\012* Do not anchor the rebuild around editing `_old` files.\\012* Do not delete the old source.\\012* Do not rename remote/CDN URLs.\\012* Rename only directly linked local CSS/JS assets you can trace safely.\\012* Use blueprint and mechanic analysis as the first decision source; use `_old` files only as fallback clarification.\\012* Stability is more important than flashy technology choices.\\012* Originality matters, but not at the cost of breaking gameplay.\\012* Presentation should be meaningfully original when mechanic safety allows.\\012* Every major rebuilt subsystem should be explainable in terms of the blueprint and the old mechanic truth.\\012* Every major presentation subsystem should be explainable in terms of the remix premise, focal identity, and authored world.\\012* Do not name temporary original-game screenshot captures with `_old.png`; use `_trash.png` instead so they can be removed at the end of the run without confusing them with preserved `_old` runtime references.\\012\\012### Testing Plan Requirement\\012\\012You must follow a compact testing plan while rebuilding.\\012\\012At minimum, test:\\012\\012* boot/load success\\012* start/play flow\\012* active gameplay loop\\012* primary controls\\012* collision/hit behavior where relevant\\012* score/progress updates where relevant\\012* fail/win/restart behavior where relevant\\012* mobile-sized usability/readability\\012* HUD clarity and CTA reachability\\012* whether the transformed presentation still communicates the real objective\\012\\012Record what was checked and what still feels fragile.\\012\\012### Suggested Artifacts\\012\\012If feasible, write:\\012\\012* `clone_surface_map.json`\\012\\012  * old path\\012  * new `_old` path\\012  * role (`entry_html`, `css`, `js`)\\012  * reference-only flag\\012* `clone_rebuild_notes.md`\\012\\012  * what was preserved\\012  * what new public surface was created\\012  * where `_old` references were actually needed\\012  * what presentation surfaces were transformed\\012* `clone_rebuild_plan.md`\\012\\012  * blueprint/mechanics/reference interaction plan\\012  * fragile surfaces\\012  * easy-update surfaces\\012  * do-not-touch conceptual surfaces\\012  * focal identity and authored-world implementation plan\\012  * chosen engine/library approach and rationale\\012* `clone_rebuild_test_plan.md`\\012\\012  * what was tested\\012  * what passed\\012  * what remains risky\\012\\012### Success Condition\\012\\012This stage succeeds when:\\012\\012* Phase 1 has already defined the blueprint\\012* a pre-build plan exists describing how blueprint, mechanics, old references, and transformation surfaces interact\\012* the old runtime has been preserved under `_old` naming\\012* a new public `index.html` exists as the canonical surface\\012* the new game has begun as a blueprint-driven rebuild\\012* `_old` files are clearly demoted to reference-only status\\012* the rebuilt surface is stability-oriented, mechanically checked, and guided by an explicit testing plan\\012* the rebuilt surface is not merely the old game with themed paint\\012* the canonical surface has a clear path toward authored world ownership, focal identity, and mobile-readable presentation\\012\\012## Phase 3 — Authored World, Design-System, and Media Mapping\\012\\012This phase enriches the rebuilt surface with mechanic-aware world semantics, design-system continuity, focal role mapping, and governed media decisions.\\012\\012Use `3d gta game` to steer narrative/world meaning, HUD language, palette logic, media mood, and scene ownership.\\012\\012This phase must convert the remix premise into a coherent playable fantasy. The player should understand what they are, what threatens them, what they want, what success means, and why the scene looks the way it does.\\012\\012### Catalog `remix_v5_world_skills.json`\\012\\012**Skill type:** `world`\\012\\012**Namespace:** `remix_v5.world`\\012\\012**Description:** Mechanic-aware authored world construction, narrative semantics, design-system planning, focal identity mapping, and progression-facing world identity.\\012\\012#### Subgroup `theme_mapping` — Mechanic-Aware Theme Mapping\\012\\012#### world-specific meanings.\\012* Label each mapping with why it is safe or where runtime verification is needed.\\012* Keep the mappings cosmetic, copy-facing, media-facing, or presentation-facing rather than logic-changing.\\012* Make the mapping visible in HUD language, entity visuals, background motifs, feedback, and progression labels where feasible.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* NONE\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* Every semantic reframe corresponds to a real gameplay surface.\\012* The world mapping preserves mechanic truth.\\012* The player-facing fantasy is coherent across the actual loop.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Theme meaning that contradicts gameplay\\012* Unsafe semantic rewrites\\012* World labels `authored_world_and_progression` — Authored World and Progression\\012\\012#### remix_v5.world.authored_world_frame — Define an authored world, not just labels\\012\\012**Intent:** Give the remix a System and Procedural Motifs\\012\\012#### remix_v5.world.remix_theme_design_system — Write a role-based `remix_theme.json`\\012\\012**Intent:** Define the design system as implementation guidance Inventory and Mapping Decisions\\012\\012#### remix_v5.media.asset_inventory_keep_replace_remap — Inventory current assets and decide keep/replace/remap\\012\\012**Intent:** Preserve the discipline of until final polish\\012\\012## Phase 2 — Direct Rebuild Phase\\012\\012This phase is the regeneration spine of the workflow. Phase 1 prepares it. Phases 3–5 enrich, realize, and prove it.\\012\\012The direct rebuild phase owns `_old` preservation, canonical new `index.html` creation, blueprint-first regeneration, subsystem-by-subsystem mechanic verification, and stability-first runtime selection.\\012\\012Use `3d gta game` here to steer how the regenerated public surface expresses mechanic meaning, authored presentation, focal identity, and stable target identity without collapsing into legacy imitation.\\012\\012The new canonical surface should not feel like a decorated copy of the old public entrypoint. It should be a stable, mechanic-faithful, public-facing regeneration that is free to rebuild presentation, UI, scene structure, and visual language wherever those surfaces are not mechanic-critical.\\012\\012### Prime Directive\\012\\012Build a new, stable, original game surface while preserving mechanic truth.\\012\\012Your output should be:\\012\\012* more original than the old source\\012* mechanically grounded in the upstream blueprint\\012* stability-first in architecture and implementation choices\\012* explicitly checked against preserved legacy references before risky rewrites land\\012* visually and semantically transformed enough to feel like a fresh public game experience\\012\\012Mechanic fidelity is mandatory. Old presentation fidelity is not mandatory unless a presentation detail is truly required for gameplay comprehension or control safety.\\012\\012### Inputs You Must Treat As Authoritative\\012\\012Use the Phase 1 outputs first:\\012\\012* mechanic decomposition\\012* protected mechanics\\012* safe theming surfaces\\012* complexity profile\\012* remix premise\\012* focal identity plan when present\\012* 1.5-level core definition\\012* five-level progression intent\\012* procedural visual identity\\012* any `remix_plan_v4.json` or equivalent planning artifact required by the current runner\\012\\012The blueprint and mechanic analysis are the main source of truth for this step.\\012\\012The old runtime is evidence, not a creative prison.\\012\\012### Hard Delivery Constraint — Single Rebuilt Public Surface\\012\\012The new game must be delivered primarily through a **single rebuilt public `index.html`**.\\012\\012Required:\\012\\012* the new public `index.html` is the canonical rebuilt surface\\012* all newly authored application code should be written inline in that same `index.html` whenever feasible\\012* inline CSS in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* inline JavaScript in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* prefer a self-contained rebuilt surface over a scattered new file graph\\012* prefer a fresh, coherent runtime surface over patched legacy presentation\\012\\012Allowed exceptions only when truly justified by stability:\\012\\012* existing local assets already required by the source game\\012* media selected from approved catalogs\\012* carefully chosen external OSS CDN libraries when they materially improve stability or execution quality\\012\\012If you use an external library, justify it briefly in your planning notes before implementation.\\012\\012### Engine / Library Selection Rule\\012\\012Before implementation, choose the most stable practical runtime approach for the job.\\012\\012Examples that may be appropriate depending on the game:\\012\\012* plain JavaScript + DOM/CSS\\012* Canvas + plain JavaScript\\012* Phaser from a stable CDN\\012* jQuery for light DOM/state glue\\012* a small combination of the above when justified\\012\\012Selection criteria in order:\\012\\0121. stability\\0122. mechanic fidelity\\0123. implementation clarity\\0124. ease of testing and repair\\0125. mobile readability and input safety\\0126. originality/expressiveness\\012\\012Do not choose a heavier engine or library just because it is fashionable.\\012\\012Use the simplest browser-native path that can produce a vivid authored result.\\012\\012### Approved Media / Library Sources\\012\\012You may use:\\012\\012* approved local audio catalogs\\012* approved local GIF/media catalogs\\012* popular open-source CDN libraries when stability and maintainability benefit\\012\\012Do not introduce random, obscure, fragile, or poorly supported dependencies.\\012\\012If stability is in doubt, prefer simpler technology.\\012\\012If visual richness can be achieved with CSS, SVG, Canvas, DOM composition, or small inline helpers, prefer that over asset-heavy substitution.\\012\\012### Mission\\012\\012Using the upstream blueprint:\\012\\0121. preserve the old runnable source under `_old` names\\0122. create a new public implementation surface\\0123. begin building an entirely new game from the blueprint/mechanics analysis\\0124. keep the `_old` files as reference-only fallback material\\0125. make the new canonical surface visibly authored, coherent, and prompt-driven\\012\\012### Mandatory Pre-Build Planning Pass\\012\\012Before you start creating the new public `index.html`, first produce a short implementation plan in the workspace describing how the blueprint and known mechanics interact with the old reference.\\012\\012That plan must:\\012\\012* cite relevant old code pieces when identifiable\\012* name the mechanic surfaces that matter most\\012* explain how the blueprint maps onto those mechanic surfaces\\012* identify what is fragile\\012* identify what is easy to update safely\\012* identify what should not be touched conceptually\\012* identify which old presentation surfaces are safe to replace or demote\\012* identify how the focal identity and authored world will appear in the new canonical surface\\012* note where `_old` reference checks are required before rewriting\\012\\012At minimum, the plan should comment on:\\012\\012* player input/control handling\\012* movement/update loop\\012* collision/hit detection\\012* scoring/progression signals\\012* fail/win state handling\\012* UI/HUD surfaces\\012* focal actor/entity representation\\012* background/scene ownership\\012* media/asset wiring\\012\\012This planning pass should exist before the main rebuild work proceeds.\\012\\012### Required Sequence\\012\\012#### A. Preserve old runtime surfaces\\012\\0121. Find the current public entrypoint, especially `index.html`.\\0122. Rename it to an `_old` form.\\012\\012   * Prefer `index_old.html`.\\0123. Inspect that preserved HTML and rename directly linked **local** CSS/JS files into `_old` forms too.\\012\\012   * Prefer `styles_old.css`, `game_old.js`, etc.\\0124. Update the preserved HTML so it still resolves correctly against the renamed `_old` assets.\\012\\012#### B. Establish the new public surface\\012\\0125. Create or overwrite a fresh public `index.html` as the new canonical implementation surface.\\0126. Start building the new game from the upstream blueprint rather than patching the old source in place.\\0127. Prefer newly authored structure, UI, art systems, scene construction, and code paths when safe.\\0128. Keep the rebuilt implementation inline in the same new `index.html` unless a clearly justified stability reason prevents it.\\0129. Make the new public surface feel like the real finished game, not a wrapper around legacy structure.\\012\\012#### C. Reference-only old surfaces\\012\\01210. Treat `_old` files as evidence/reference only.\\01211. Inspect them only when:\\012\\012* mechanic behavior is ambiguous\\012* edge-case expectations are unclear\\012* you need to avoid accidental mechanic drift\\012* you need to confirm that a presentation change will not break a real gameplay expectation\\012\\012#### D. Component-by-component verification during rewrite\\012\\01212. For each rewritten component or mechanic-facing subsystem, compare it against the old reference before finalizing.\\012\\012This includes, where relevant:\\012\\012* control/input behavior\\012* animation/update timing\\012* collision/contact behavior\\012* score/progress reporting\\012* fail/win transitions\\012* HUD feedback\\012* mobile tap/click paths\\012* gameplay-critical visibility\\012\\012If a rewritten component is more original but less stable, less testable, or mechanically less truthful, revise it.\\012\\012If a rewritten component is mechanically safe but visually generic, under-authored, or too similar to the old surface, strengthen the presentation before final handoff.\\012\\012### Rules\\012\\012* Do not let `_old` files remain the main implementation surface.\\012* Do not anchor the rebuild around editing `_old` files.\\012* Do not delete the old source.\\012* Do not rename remote/CDN URLs.\\012* Rename only directly linked local CSS/JS assets you can trace safely.\\012* Use blueprint and mechanic analysis as the first decision source; use `_old` files only as fallback clarification.\\012* Stability is more important than flashy technology choices.\\012* Originality matters, but not at the cost of breaking gameplay.\\012* Presentation should be meaningfully original when mechanic safety allows.\\012* Every major rebuilt subsystem should be explainable in terms of the blueprint and the old mechanic truth.\\012* Every major presentation subsystem should be explainable in terms of the remix premise, focal identity, and authored world.\\012* Do not name temporary original-game screenshot captures with `_old.png`; use `_trash.png` instead so they can be removed at the end of the run without confusing them with preserved `_old` runtime references.\\012\\012### Testing Plan Requirement\\012\\012You must follow a compact testing plan while rebuilding.\\012\\012At minimum, test:\\012\\012* boot/load success\\012* start/play flow\\012* active gameplay loop\\012* primary controls\\012* collision/hit behavior where relevant\\012* score/progress updates where relevant\\012* fail/win/restart behavior where relevant\\012* mobile-sized usability/readability\\012* HUD clarity and CTA reachability\\012* whether the transformed presentation still communicates the real objective\\012\\012Record what was checked and what still feels fragile.\\012\\012### Suggested Artifacts\\012\\012If feasible, write:\\012\\012* `clone_surface_map.json`\\012\\012  * old path\\012  * new `_old` path\\012  * role (`entry_html`, `css`, `js`)\\012  * reference-only flag\\012* `clone_rebuild_notes.md`\\012\\012  * what was preserved\\012  * what new public surface was created\\012  * where `_old` references were actually needed\\012  * what presentation surfaces were transformed\\012* `clone_rebuild_plan.md`\\012\\012  * blueprint/mechanics/reference interaction plan\\012  * fragile surfaces\\012  * easy-update surfaces\\012  * do-not-touch conceptual surfaces\\012  * focal identity and authored-world implementation plan\\012  * chosen engine/library approach and rationale\\012* `clone_rebuild_test_plan.md`\\012\\012  * what was tested\\012  * what passed\\012  * what remains risky\\012\\012### Success Condition\\012\\012This stage succeeds when:\\012\\012* Phase 1 has already defined the blueprint\\012* a pre-build plan exists describing how blueprint, mechanics, old references, and transformation surfaces interact\\012* the old runtime has been preserved under `_old` naming\\012* a new public `index.html` exists as the canonical surface\\012* the new game has begun as a blueprint-driven rebuild\\012* `_old` files are clearly demoted to reference-only status\\012* the rebuilt surface is stability-oriented, mechanically checked, and guided by an explicit testing plan\\012* the rebuilt surface is not merely the old game with themed paint\\012* the canonical surface has a clear path toward authored world ownership, focal identity, and mobile-readable presentation\\012\\012## Phase 3 — Authored World, Design-System, and Media language, authored scene motifs, and focal identity.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* NONE\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* The final game looks and feels like a meaningfully different authored identity.\\012* Conservative mechanics do not result in conservative presentation.\\012* The visual and semantic transformation is visible beyond text and color changes.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Timid surface edits\\012* “Same game, new labels” output\\012* Generic themed reskin\\012* Keeping everything basically the same because mechanics were preserved\\012\\012#### remix_v5.core.mobile_first_runtime_discipline — Stay mobile-first and runtime-disciplined\\012\\012**Intent:** Preserve the mobile-first operational posture across all phases, including runtime validation and screenshot capture.\\012\\012**Required actions:**\\012\\012* Assume the primary validation target is a mobile portrait viewport.\\012* Keep controls reachable, CTA paths visible, labels readable, and overlays non-blocking.\\012* Preserve gameplay space and avoid decorative chrome that crowds touch targets.\\012* Use the assigned validation/runtime channel only when browser-grounded evidence is needed.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* NONE\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* The remixed game is actionable on mobile.\\012* HUD, controls, CTAs, and modal states are readable and reachable.\\012* Validation evidence comes from the assigned runtime rather than assumptions.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Desktop-only optimization\\012* Broken touch flows\\012* Fake or unrelated runtime evidence\\012* Mobile visual polish that blocks playability\\012\\012#### Subgroup `workspace_and_catalog_discipline` — Workspace and Catalog Discipline\\012\\012#### remix_v5.core.catalogs_are_read_only — Treat catalogs as read-only authority\\012\\012**Intent:** Use `catalogs/` as both mechanic preservation and transformation quality.\\012* Temporary original-game reference captures are clearly disposable by filename.\\012\\012**Failure modes prevented:**\\012\\012* Fake screenshots\\012* Missing contract files\\012* Narrative-only reporting without implementation evidence\\012* Claims of transformation unsupported by runtime proof\\012* Temporary reference captures being mistaken for preserved legacy runtime files\\012\\012#### Subgroup `execution_style` — Execution Style\\012\\012#### remix_v5.core.no_lazy_prompt_collapse — Do not collapse into a lazy checks.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* NONE\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* The operator can explain why each transformation happened.\\012* The final prompt remains inspectable mismatch\\012* Asset soup\\012* Focal identity disconnected from gameplay roles\\012\\012## Phase 1 — Source Truth, Blueprint, and Progression Planning\\012\\012This phase prepares the regeneration asked to become without losing mechanic truth.\\012\\012This phase must distinguish between what must be preserved mechanically and what should be transformed aggressively in Progression\\012\\012#### remix_v5.analysis.complexity_profile_and_safe_escalation — Assess true complexity and safe escalation knobs\\012\\012**Intent:** Determine what kind of game this actually is Subgroup `progressive_disclosure_reasoning` — Progressive Disclosure Reasoning\\012\\012#### remix_v5.analysis.progressive_disclosure_and_complexity_rationale — Preserve progressive-disclosure difficulty\\012\\012#### Subgroup `analysis_artifacts_and_handoff` — Analysis Artifacts and Handoff\\012\\012#### remix_v5.analysis.procedural_art_system_and_downstream_contract — Plan the procedural until final polish\\012\\012## Phase 2 — Direct Rebuild Phase\\012\\012This phase is the regeneration spine of the workflow. Phase 1 prepares it. Phases 3–5 enrich, realize, and prove it.\\012\\012The direct rebuild phase owns `_old` preservation, canonical new `index.html` creation, blueprint-first regeneration, subsystem-by-subsystem mechanic verification, and stability-first runtime selection.\\012\\012Use `Create a deterministic creative remix in a Apex Legends inspired style, centered on a talking sponge, but make it futuristic. Preserve the core playable mechanic loop while rebuilding the theme, identity, surface art, world language, and presentation around this new premise.` here to steer how the regenerated public surface expresses mechanic meaning, authored presentation, focal identity, and stable target identity without collapsing into legacy imitation.\\012\\012The new canonical surface should not feel like a decorated copy of the old public entrypoint. It should be a stable, mechanic-faithful, public-facing regeneration that is free to rebuild presentation, UI, scene structure, and visual language wherever those surfaces are not mechanic-critical.\\012\\012### Prime Directive\\012\\012Build a new, stable, original game surface while preserving mechanic truth.\\012\\012Your output should be:\\012\\012* more original than the old source\\012* mechanically grounded in the upstream blueprint\\012* stability-first in architecture and implementation choices\\012* explicitly checked against preserved legacy references before risky rewrites land\\012* visually and semantically transformed enough to feel like a fresh public game experience\\012\\012Mechanic fidelity is mandatory. Old presentation fidelity is not mandatory unless a presentation detail is truly required for gameplay comprehension or control safety.\\012\\012### Inputs You Must Treat As Authoritative\\012\\012Use the Phase 1 outputs first:\\012\\012* mechanic decomposition\\012* protected mechanics\\012* safe theming surfaces\\012* complexity profile\\012* remix premise\\012* focal identity plan when present\\012* 1.5-level core definition\\012* five-level progression intent\\012* procedural visual identity\\012* any `remix_plan_v4.json` or equivalent planning artifact required by the current runner\\012\\012The blueprint and mechanic analysis are the main source of truth for this step.\\012\\012The old runtime is evidence, not a creative prison.\\012\\012### Hard Delivery Constraint — Single Rebuilt Public Surface\\012\\012The new game must be delivered primarily through a **single rebuilt public `index.html`**.\\012\\012Required:\\012\\012* the new public `index.html` is the canonical rebuilt surface\\012* all newly authored application code should be written inline in that same `index.html` whenever feasible\\012* inline CSS in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* inline JavaScript in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* prefer a self-contained rebuilt surface over a scattered new file graph\\012* prefer a fresh, coherent runtime surface over patched legacy presentation\\012\\012Allowed exceptions only when truly justified by stability:\\012\\012* existing local assets already required by the source game\\012* media selected from approved catalogs\\012* carefully chosen external OSS CDN libraries when they materially improve stability or execution quality\\012\\012If you use an external library, justify it briefly in your planning notes before implementation.\\012\\012### Engine / Library Selection Rule\\012\\012Before implementation, choose the most stable practical runtime approach for the job.\\012\\012Examples that may be appropriate depending on the game:\\012\\012* plain JavaScript + DOM/CSS\\012* Canvas + plain JavaScript\\012* Phaser from a stable CDN\\012* jQuery for light DOM/state glue\\012* a small combination of the above when justified\\012\\012Selection criteria in order:\\012\\0121. stability\\0122. mechanic fidelity\\0123. implementation clarity\\0124. ease of testing and repair\\0125. mobile readability and input safety\\0126. originality/expressiveness\\012\\012Do not choose a heavier engine or library just because it is fashionable.\\012\\012Use the simplest browser-native path that can produce a vivid authored result.\\012\\012### Approved Media / Library Sources\\012\\012You may use:\\012\\012* approved local audio catalogs\\012* approved local GIF/media catalogs\\012* popular open-source CDN libraries when stability and maintainability benefit\\012\\012Do not introduce random, obscure, fragile, or poorly supported dependencies.\\012\\012If stability is in doubt, prefer simpler technology.\\012\\012If visual richness can be achieved with CSS, SVG, Canvas, DOM composition, or small inline helpers, prefer that over asset-heavy substitution.\\012\\012### Mission\\012\\012Using the upstream blueprint:\\012\\0121. preserve the old runnable source under `_old` names\\0122. create a new public implementation surface\\0123. begin building an entirely new game from the blueprint/mechanics analysis\\0124. keep the `_old` files as reference-only fallback material\\0125. make the new canonical surface visibly authored, coherent, and prompt-driven\\012\\012### Mandatory Pre-Build Planning Pass\\012\\012Before you start creating the new public `index.html`, first produce a short implementation plan in the workspace describing how the blueprint and known mechanics interact with the old reference.\\012\\012That plan must:\\012\\012* cite relevant old code pieces when identifiable\\012* name the mechanic surfaces that matter most\\012* explain how the blueprint maps onto those mechanic surfaces\\012* identify what is fragile\\012* identify what is easy to update safely\\012* identify what should not be touched conceptually\\012* identify which old presentation surfaces are safe to replace or demote\\012* identify how the focal identity and authored world will appear in the new canonical surface\\012* note where `_old` reference checks are required before rewriting\\012\\012At minimum, the plan should comment on:\\012\\012* player input/control handling\\012* movement/update loop\\012* collision/hit detection\\012* scoring/progression signals\\012* fail/win state handling\\012* UI/HUD surfaces\\012* focal actor/entity representation\\012* background/scene ownership\\012* media/asset wiring\\012\\012This planning pass should exist before the main rebuild work proceeds.\\012\\012### Required Sequence\\012\\012#### A. Preserve old runtime surfaces\\012\\0121. Find the current public entrypoint, especially `index.html`.\\0122. Rename it to an `_old` form.\\012\\012   * Prefer `index_old.html`.\\0123. Inspect that preserved HTML and rename directly linked **local** CSS/JS files into `_old` forms too.\\012\\012   * Prefer `styles_old.css`, `game_old.js`, etc.\\0124. Update the preserved HTML so it still resolves correctly against the renamed `_old` assets.\\012\\012#### B. Establish the new public surface\\012\\0125. Create or overwrite a fresh public `index.html` as the new canonical implementation surface.\\0126. Start building the new game from the upstream blueprint rather than patching the old source in place.\\0127. Prefer newly authored structure, UI, art systems, scene construction, and code paths when safe.\\0128. Keep the rebuilt implementation inline in the same new `index.html` unless a clearly justified stability reason prevents it.\\0129. Make the new public surface feel like the real finished game, not a wrapper around legacy structure.\\012\\012#### C. Reference-only old surfaces\\012\\01210. Treat `_old` files as evidence/reference only.\\01211. Inspect them only when:\\012\\012* mechanic behavior is ambiguous\\012* edge-case expectations are unclear\\012* you need to avoid accidental mechanic drift\\012* you need to confirm that a presentation change will not break a real gameplay expectation\\012\\012#### D. Component-by-component verification during rewrite\\012\\01212. For each rewritten component or mechanic-facing subsystem, compare it against the old reference before finalizing.\\012\\012This includes, where relevant:\\012\\012* control/input behavior\\012* animation/update timing\\012* collision/contact behavior\\012* score/progress reporting\\012* fail/win transitions\\012* HUD feedback\\012* mobile tap/click paths\\012* gameplay-critical visibility\\012\\012If a rewritten component is more original but less stable, less testable, or mechanically less truthful, revise it.\\012\\012If a rewritten component is mechanically safe but visually generic, under-authored, or too similar to the old surface, strengthen the presentation before final handoff.\\012\\012### Rules\\012\\012* Do not let `_old` files remain the main implementation surface.\\012* Do not anchor the rebuild around editing `_old` files.\\012* Do not delete the old source.\\012* Do not rename remote/CDN URLs.\\012* Rename only directly linked local CSS/JS assets you can trace safely.\\012* Use blueprint and mechanic analysis as the first decision source; use `_old` files only as fallback clarification.\\012* Stability is more important than flashy technology choices.\\012* Originality matters, but not at the cost of breaking gameplay.\\012* Presentation should be meaningfully original when mechanic safety allows.\\012* Every major rebuilt subsystem should be explainable in terms of the blueprint and the old mechanic truth.\\012* Every major presentation subsystem should be explainable in terms of the remix premise, focal identity, and authored world.\\012* Do not name temporary original-game screenshot captures with `_old.png`; use `_trash.png` instead so they can be removed at the end of the run without confusing them with preserved `_old` runtime references.\\012\\012### Testing Plan Requirement\\012\\012You must follow a compact testing plan while rebuilding.\\012\\012At minimum, test:\\012\\012* boot/load success\\012* start/play flow\\012* active gameplay loop\\012* primary controls\\012* collision/hit behavior where relevant\\012* score/progress updates where relevant\\012* fail/win/restart behavior where relevant\\012* mobile-sized usability/readability\\012* HUD clarity and CTA reachability\\012* whether the transformed presentation still communicates the real objective\\012\\012Record what was checked and what still feels fragile.\\012\\012### Suggested Artifacts\\012\\012If feasible, write:\\012\\012* `clone_surface_map.json`\\012\\012  * old path\\012  * new `_old` path\\012  * role (`entry_html`, `css`, `js`)\\012  * reference-only flag\\012* `clone_rebuild_notes.md`\\012\\012  * what was preserved\\012  * what new public surface was created\\012  * where `_old` references were actually needed\\012  * what presentation surfaces were transformed\\012* `clone_rebuild_plan.md`\\012\\012  * blueprint/mechanics/reference interaction plan\\012  * fragile surfaces\\012  * easy-update surfaces\\012  * do-not-touch conceptual surfaces\\012  * focal identity and authored-world implementation plan\\012  * chosen engine/library approach and rationale\\012* `clone_rebuild_test_plan.md`\\012\\012  * what was tested\\012  * what passed\\012  * what remains risky\\012\\012### Success Condition\\012\\012This stage succeeds when:\\012\\012* Phase 1 has already defined the blueprint\\012* a pre-build plan exists describing how blueprint, mechanics, old references, and transformation surfaces interact\\012* the old runtime has been preserved under `_old` naming\\012* a new public `index.html` exists as the canonical surface\\012* the new game has begun as a blueprint-driven rebuild\\012* `_old` files are clearly demoted to reference-only status\\012* the rebuilt surface is stability-oriented, mechanically checked, and guided by an explicit testing plan\\012* the rebuilt surface is not merely the old game with themed paint\\012* the canonical surface has a clear path toward authored world ownership, focal identity, and mobile-readable presentation\\012\\012## Phase 3 — Authored World, Design-System, and Media Mapping\\012\\012This phase enriches the rebuilt surface with mechanic-aware world semantics, design-system continuity, focal role mapping, and governed media decisions.\\012\\012Use `Create a deterministic creative remix in a Apex Legends inspired style, centered on a talking sponge, but make it futuristic. Preserve the core playable mechanic loop while rebuilding the theme, identity, surface art, world language, and presentation around this new premise.` to steer narrative/world meaning, HUD language, palette logic, media mood, and scene ownership.\\012\\012This phase must convert the remix premise into a coherent playable fantasy. The player should understand what they are, what threatens them, what they want, what success means, and why the scene looks the way it does.\\012\\012### Catalog `remix_v5_world_skills.json`\\012\\012**Skill type:** `world`\\012\\012**Namespace:** `remix_v5.world`\\012\\012**Description:** Mechanic-aware authored world construction, narrative semantics, design-system planning, focal identity mapping, and progression-facing world identity.\\012\\012#### Subgroup `theme_mapping` — Mechanic-Aware Theme Mapping\\012\\012#### remix_v5.world.mechanic_aware_semantic_mapping — Map mechanics into themed world semantics\\012\\012**Intent:** Translate avatar, hazards, rewards, goals, score, and failure semantics into the remix world without changing the underlying mechanics.\\012\\012**Required actions:**\\012\\012* Map player, hazards, collectibles, goals, timers, score, progress, win states, and failure states into world-specific meanings.\\012* Label each mapping with why it is safe or where runtime verification is needed.\\012* Keep the mappings cosmetic, copy-facing, media-facing, or presentation-facing rather than logic-changing.\\012* Make the mapping visible in HUD language, entity visuals, background motifs, feedback, and progression labels where feasible.\\012\\012**Required artifacts:**\\012\\012* NONE\\012\\012**Acceptance bar:**\\012\\012* Every semantic reframe corresponds to a real gameplay surface.\\012* The world mapping preserves mechanic truth.\\012* The Validation\\012\\012This phase proves the rebuilt game with runtime evidence, deterministic repair, before/after comparison, and optional family-level validation when multiple playable surfaces exist.\\012\\012Use `Create a deterministic creative remix in a Apex Legends inspired style, centered on a talking sponge, but make it futuristic. Preserve the core playable mechanic loop while rebuilding the theme, identity, surface art, world language, and presentation around this new premise.` as an explicit judging lens, not just a setup input.\\012\\012Runtime proof must validate both mechanic truth and transformation quality. Start building the new game from the upstream blueprint rather than patching the old source in place.\\0127. Prefer newly authored structure, UI, art systems, scene construction, and code paths when safe.\\0128. Keep the rebuilt implementation inline in the same new `index.html` unless a clearly justified stability reason prevents it.\\0129. Make the new public surface feel like the real finished game, not a wrapper around legacy structure.\\012\\012#### C. Reference-only old surfaces\\012\\01210. Treat `_old` files as evidence/reference only.\\01211. Inspect them only when:\\012\\012* mechanic behavior is ambiguous\\012* edge-case expectations are unclear\\012* you need to avoid accidental mechanic drift\\012* you need to confirm that a presentation change will not break a real gameplay expectation\\012\\012#### D. Component-by-component verification during rewrite\\012\\01212. For each rewritten component or mechanic-facing subsystem, compare it against the old reference before finalizing.\\012\\012This includes, where relevant:\\012\\012* control/input behavior\\012* animation/update timing\\012* collision/contact behavior\\012* score/progress reporting\\012* fail/win transitions\\012* HUD feedback\\012* mobile tap/click paths\\012* gameplay-critical visibility\\012\\012If a rewritten component is more original but less stable, less testable, or mechanically less truthful, revise it.\\012\\012If a rewritten component is mechanically safe but visually generic, under-authored, or too similar to the old surface, strengthen the presentation before final handoff.\\012\\012### Rules\\012\\012* Do not let `_old` files remain the main implementation surface.\\012* Do not anchor the rebuild around editing `_old` files.\\012* Do not delete the old source.\\012* Do not rename remote/CDN URLs.\\012* Rename only directly linked local CSS/JS assets you can trace safely.\\012* Use blueprint and mechanic analysis as the first decision source; use `_old` files only as fallback clarification.\\012* Stability is more important than flashy technology choices.\\012* Originality matters, but not at the cost of breaking gameplay.\\012* Presentation should be meaningfully original when mechanic safety allows.\\012* Every major rebuilt subsystem should be explainable in terms of the blueprint and the old mechanic truth.\\012* Every major presentation subsystem should be explainable in terms of the remix premise, focal identity, and authored world.\\012* Do not name temporary original-game screenshot captures with `_old.png`; use `_trash.png` instead so they can be removed at the end of the run without confusing them with preserved `_old` runtime references.\\012\\012### Testing Plan Requirement\\012\\012You must follow a compact testing plan while rebuilding.\\012\\012At minimum, test:\\012\\012* boot/load success\\012* start/play flow\\012* active gameplay loop\\012* primary controls\\012* collision/hit behavior where relevant\\012* score/progress updates where relevant\\012* fail/win/restart behavior where relevant\\012* mobile-sized usability/readability\\012* HUD clarity and CTA reachability\\012* whether the transformed presentation still communicates the real objective\\012\\012Record what was checked and what still feels fragile.\\012\\012### Suggested Artifacts\\012\\012If feasible, write:\\012\\012* `clone_surface_map.json`\\012\\012  * old path\\012  * new `_old` path\\012  * role (`entry_html`, `css`, `js`)\\012  * reference-only flag\\012* `clone_rebuild_notes.md`\\012\\012  * what was preserved\\012  * what new public surface was created\\012  * where `_old` references were actually needed\\012  * what presentation surfaces were transformed\\012* `clone_rebuild_plan.md`\\012\\012  * blueprint/mechanics/reference interaction plan\\012  * fragile surfaces\\012  * easy-update surfaces\\012  * do-not-touch conceptual surfaces\\012  * focal identity and authored-world implementation plan\\012  * chosen engine/library approach and rationale\\012* `clone_rebuild_test_plan.md`\\012\\012  * what was tested\\012  * what passed\\012  * what remains risky\\012\\012### Success Condition\\012\\012This stage succeeds when:\\012\\012* Phase 1 has already defined the blueprint\\012* a pre-build plan exists describing how blueprint, mechanics, old references, and transformation surfaces interact\\012* the old runtime has been preserved under `_old` naming\\012* a new public `index.html` exists as the canonical surface\\012* the new game has begun as a blueprint-driven rebuild\\012* `_old` files are clearly demoted to reference-only status\\012* the rebuilt surface is stability-oriented, mechanically checked, and guided by an explicit testing plan\\012* the rebuilt surface is not merely the old game with themed paint\\012* the canonical surface has a clear path toward authored world ownership, focal identity, and mobile-readable presentation\\012\\012## Phase 3 — Authored World, Design-System, and Media merged source prompts\\012* Unstructured creativity that cannot be debugged\\012* Generic “be creative” behavior with no operational teeth\\012\\012#### remix_v5.core.cross_phase_consistency — Keep all phases aligned\\012\\012**Intent:** Ensure analysis, world, visual, media, and QA outputs describe the same remixed game.\\012\\012**Required actions:**\\012\\012* Keep terminology stable across mismatch\\012* Asset soup\\012* Focal identity disconnected from gameplay roles\\012\\012## Phase 1 — Source Truth, Blueprint, and Progression Planning\\012\\012This phase prepares the regeneration spine by establishing current-game truth, protected mechanics, safe theming surfaces, progression logic, focal identity opportunities, and downstream contracts.\\012\\012Use `Create a deterministic creative remix in a Studio Ghibli inspired style, centered on a roller disco star, but make it street. asked to become without losing mechanic truth.\\012\\012This phase must distinguish between what must be preserved mechanically and what should be transformed aggressively in until final polish\\012\\012## Phase 2 — Direct Rebuild Phase\\012\\012This phase is the regeneration spine of the workflow. Phase 1 prepares it. Phases 3–5 enrich, realize, and prove it.\\012\\012The direct rebuild phase owns `_old` preservation, canonical new `index.html` creation, blueprint-first regeneration, subsystem-by-subsystem mechanic verification, and stability-first runtime selection.\\012\\012Use `Create a deterministic creative remix in a Studio Ghibli inspired style, centered on a roller disco star, but make it street. Preserve the core playable mechanic loop while rebuilding the theme, identity, surface art, world language, and presentation around this new premise.` here to steer how the regenerated public surface expresses mechanic meaning, authored presentation, focal identity, and stable target identity without collapsing into legacy imitation.\\012\\012The new canonical surface should not feel like a decorated copy of the old public entrypoint. It should be a stable, mechanic-faithful, public-facing regeneration that is free to rebuild presentation, UI, scene structure, and visual language wherever those surfaces are not mechanic-critical.\\012\\012### Prime Directive\\012\\012Build a new, stable, original game surface while preserving mechanic truth.\\012\\012Your output should be:\\012\\012* more original than the old source\\012* mechanically grounded in the upstream blueprint\\012* stability-first in architecture and implementation choices\\012* explicitly checked against preserved legacy references before risky rewrites land\\012* visually and semantically transformed enough to feel like a fresh public game experience\\012\\012Mechanic fidelity is mandatory. Old presentation fidelity is not mandatory unless a presentation detail is truly required for gameplay comprehension or control safety.\\012\\012### Inputs You Must Treat As Authoritative\\012\\012Use the Phase 1 outputs first:\\012\\012* mechanic decomposition\\012* protected mechanics\\012* safe theming surfaces\\012* complexity profile\\012* remix premise\\012* focal identity plan when present\\012* 1.5-level core definition\\012* five-level progression intent\\012* procedural visual identity\\012* any `remix_plan_v4.json` or equivalent planning artifact required by the current runner\\012\\012The blueprint and mechanic analysis are the main source of truth for this step.\\012\\012The old runtime is evidence, not a creative prison.\\012\\012### Hard Delivery Constraint — Single Rebuilt Public Surface\\012\\012The new game must be delivered primarily through a **single rebuilt public `index.html`**.\\012\\012Required:\\012\\012* the new public `index.html` is the canonical rebuilt surface\\012* all newly authored application code should be written inline in that same `index.html` whenever feasible\\012* inline CSS in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* inline JavaScript in the rebuilt `index.html`\\012* prefer a self-contained rebuilt surface over a scattered new file graph\\012* prefer a fresh, coherent runtime surface over patched legacy presentation\\012\\012Allowed exceptions only when truly justified by stability:\\012\\012* existing local assets already required by the source game\\012* media selected from approved catalogs\\012* carefully chosen external OSS CDN libraries when they materially improve stability or execution quality\\012\\012If you use an external library, justify it briefly in your planning notes before implementation.\\012\\012### Engine / Library Selection Rule\\012\\012Before implementation, choose the most stable practical runtime approach for the job.\\012\\012Examples that may be appropriate depending on the game:\\012\\012* plain JavaScript + DOM/CSS\\012* Canvas + plain JavaScript\\012* Phaser from a stable CDN\\012* jQuery for light DOM/state glue\\012* a small combination of the above when justified\\012\\012Selection criteria in order:\\012\\0121. stability\\0122. mechanic fidelity\\0123. implementation clarity\\0124. ease of testing and repair\\0125. mobile readability and input safety\\0126. originality/expressiveness\\012\\012Do not choose a heavier engine or library just because it is fashionable.\\012\\012Use the simplest browser-native path that can produce a vivid authored result.\\012\\012### Approved Media / Library Sources\\012\\012You may use:\\012\\012* approved local audio catalogs\\012* approved local GIF/media catalogs\\012* popular open-source CDN libraries when stability and maintainability benefit\\012\\012Do not introduce random, obscure, fragile, or poorly supported dependencies.\\012\\012If stability is in doubt, prefer simpler technology.\\012\\012If visual richness can be achieved with CSS, SVG, Canvas, DOM composition, or small inline helpers, prefer that over asset-heavy substitution.\\012\\012### Mission\\012\\012Using the upstream blueprint:\\012\\0121. preserve the old runnable source under `_old` names\\0122. create a new public implementation surface\\0123. begin building an entirely new game from the blueprint/mechanics analysis\\0124. keep the `_old` files as reference-only fallback material\\0125. make the new canonical surface visibly authored, coherent, and prompt-driven\\012\\012### Mandatory Pre-Build Planning Pass\\012\\012Before you start creating the new public `index.html`, first produce a short implementation plan in the workspace describing how the blueprint and known mechanics interact with the old reference.\\012\\012That plan must:\\012\\012* cite relevant old code pieces when identifiable\\012* name the mechanic surfaces that matter most\\012* explain how the blueprint maps onto those mechanic surfaces\\012* identify what is fragile\\012* identify what is easy to update safely\\012* identify what should not be touched conceptually\\012* identify which old presentation surfaces are safe to replace or demote\\012* identify how the focal identity and authored world will appear in the new canonical surface\\012* note where `_old` reference checks are required before rewriting\\012\\012At minimum, the plan should comment on:\\012\\012* player input/control handling\\012* movement/update loop\\012* collision/hit detection\\012* scoring/progression signals\\012* fail/win state handling\\012* UI/HUD surfaces\\012* focal actor/entity representation\\012* background/scene ownership\\012* media/asset wiring\\012\\012This planning pass should exist before the main rebuild work proceeds.\\012\\012### Required Sequence\\012\\012#### A. Preserve old runtime surfaces\\012\\0121. Find the current public entrypoint, especially `index.html`.\\0122. Rename it to an `_old` form.\\012\\012   * Prefer `index_old.html`.\\0123. Inspect that preserved HTML and rename directly linked **local** CSS/JS files into `_old` forms too.\\012\\012   * Prefer `styles_old.css`, `game_old.js`, etc.\\0124. Update the preserved HTML so it still resolves correctly against the renamed `_old` assets.\\012\\012#### B. Establish the new public surface\\012\\0125. Create or overwrite a fresh public `index.html` as the new canonical implementation surface.\\0126. Start building the new game from the upstream blueprint rather than patching the old source in place.\\0127. Prefer newly authored structure, UI, art systems, scene construction, and code paths when safe.\\0128. Keep the rebuilt implementation inline in the same new `index.html` unless a clearly justified stability reason prevents it.\\0129. Make the new public surface feel like the real finished game, not a wrapper around legacy structure.\\012\\012#### C. Reference-only old surfaces\\012\\01210. Treat `_old` files as evidence/reference only.\\01211. Inspect them only when:\\012\\012* mechanic behavior is ambiguous\\012* edge-case expectations are unclear\\012* you need to avoid accidental mechanic drift\\012* you need to confirm that a presentation change will not break a real gameplay expectation\\012\\012#### D. Component-by-component verification during rewrite\\012\\01212. For each rewritten component or mechanic-facing subsystem, compare it against the old reference before finalizing.\\012\\012This includes, where relevant:\\012\\012* control/input behavior\\012* animation/update timing\\012* collision/contact behavior\\012* score/progress reporting\\012* fail/win transitions\\012* HUD feedback\\012* mobile tap/click paths\\012* gameplay-critical visibility\\012\\012If a rewritten component is more original but less stable, less testable, or mechanically less truthful, revise it.\\012\\012If a rewritten component is mechanically safe but visually generic, under-authored, or too similar to the old surface, strengthen the presentation before final handoff.\\012\\012### Rules\\012\\012* Do not let `_old` files remain the main implementation surface.\\012* Do not anchor the rebuild around editing `_old` files.\\012* Do not delete the old source.\\012* Do not rename remote/CDN URLs.\\012* Rename only directly linked local CSS/JS assets you can trace safely.\\012* Use blueprint and mechanic analysis as the first decision source; use `_old` files only as fallback clarification.\\012* Stability is more important than flashy technology choices.\\012* Originality matters, but not at the cost of breaking gameplay.\\012* Presentation should be meaningfully original when mechanic safety allows.\\012* Every major rebuilt subsystem should be explainable in terms of the blueprint and the old mechanic truth.\\012* Every major presentation subsystem should be explainable in terms of the remix premise, focal identity, and authored world.\\012* Do not name temporary original-game screenshot captures with `_old.png`; use `_trash.png` instead so they can be removed at the end of the run without confusing them with preserved `_old` runtime references.\\012\\012### Testing Plan Requirement\\012\\012You must follow a compact testing plan while rebuilding.\\012\\012At minimum, test:\\012\\012* boot/load success\\012* start/play flow\\012* active gameplay loop\\012* primary controls\\012* collision/hit behavior where relevant\\012* score/progress updates where relevant\\012* fail/win/restart behavior where relevant\\012* mobile-sized usability/readability\\012* HUD clarity and CTA reachability\\012* whether the transformed presentation still communicates the real objective\\012\\012Record what was checked and what still feels fragile.\\012\\012### Suggested Artifacts\\012\\012If feasible, write:\\012\\012* `clone_surface_map.json`\\012\\012  * old path\\012  * new `_old` path\\012  * role (`entry_html`, `css`, `js`)\\012  * reference-only flag\\012* `clone_rebuild_notes.md`\\012\\012  * what was preserved\\012  * what new public surface was created\\012  * where `_old` references were actually needed\\012  * what presentation surfaces were transformed\\012* `clone_rebuild_plan.md`\\012\\012  * blueprint/mechanics/reference interaction plan\\012  * fragile surfaces\\012  * easy-update surfaces\\012  * do-not-touch conceptual surfaces\\012  * focal identity and authored-world implementation plan\\012  * chosen engine/library approach and rationale\\012* `clone_rebuild_test_plan.md`\\012\\012  * what was tested\\012  * what passed\\012  * what remains risky\\012\\012### Success Condition\\012\\012This stage succeeds when:\\012\\012* Phase 1 has already defined the blueprint\\012* a pre-build plan exists describing how blueprint, mechanics, old references, and transformation surfaces interact\\012* the old runtime has been preserved under `_old` naming\\012* a new public `index.html` exists as the canonical surface\\012* the new game has begun as a blueprint-driven rebuild\\012* `_old` files are clearly demoted to reference-only status\\012* the rebuilt surface is stability-oriented, mechanically checked, and guided by an explicit testing plan\\012* the rebuilt surface is not merely the old game with themed paint\\012* the canonical surface has a clear path toward authored world ownership, focal identity, and mobile-readable presentation\\012\\012## Phase 3 — Authored World, Design-System, and Media authored result.\\012\\012### Approved Media / Library Sources\\012\\012You may use:\\012\\012* approved local audio catalogs\\012* approved local GIF/media catalogs\\012* popular open-source CDN technology.\\012\\012If visual richness can be achieved with CSS, SVG, Canvas, DOM composition, or small inline helpers, prefer that over asset-heavy substitution.\\012\\012### Mission\\012\\012Using the upstream blueprint:\\012\\0121. preserve the old runnable source under `_old` names\\0122. create a new public implementation surface\\0123. begin building an entirely new game from the blueprint/mechanics analysis\\0124. keep the `_old` files as reference-only fallback material\\0125. make the new canonical surface visibly authored, coherent, and prompt-driven\\012\\012### Mandatory Pre-Build Planning Pass\\012\\012Before you start creating the new public `index.html`, first produce a short implementation plan in the workspace describing how the blueprint and known mechanics interact with the old reference.\\012\\012That plan must:\\012\\012* cite relevant old code pieces when identifiable\\012* name the mechanic surfaces that matter most\\012* explain how the blueprint maps onto those mechanic surfaces\\012* identify what is fragile\\012* identify what is easy to update safely\\012* identify what should not be touched conceptually\\012* identify which old presentation surfaces are safe to replace or demote\\012* identify how the focal identity and authored world will appear in the new canonical surface\\012* note where `_old` reference checks are required before rewriting\\012\\012At minimum, the plan should comment on:\\012\\012* player input/control handling\\012* movement/update loop\\012* collision/hit detection\\012* scoring/progression signals\\012* fail/win state handling\\012* UI/HUD surfaces\\012* focal actor/entity representation\\012* background/scene ownership\\012* media/asset wiring\\012\\012This planning pass should exist before the main rebuild work proceeds.\\012\\012### Required Sequence\\012\\012#### A. Preserve old runtime surfaces\\012\\0121. Find the current public entrypoint, especially `index.html`.\\0122. Rename it to an `_old` form.\\012\\012   * Prefer `index_old.html`.\\0123. Inspect that preserved HTML and rename directly linked **local** CSS/JS files into `_old` forms too.\\012\\012   * Prefer `styles_old.css`, `game_old.js`, etc.\\0124. Update the preserved HTML so it still resolves correctly against the renamed `_old` assets.\\012\\012#### B. Establish the new public surface\\012\\0125. Create or overwrite a fresh public `index.html` as the new canonical implementation surface.\\0126. Start building the new game from the upstream blueprint rather than patching the old source in place.\\0127. Prefer newly authored structure, UI, art systems, scene construction, and code paths when safe.\\0128. Keep the rebuilt implementation inline in the same new `index.html` unless a clearly justified stability reason prevents it.\\0129. Make the new public surface feel like the real finished game, not a wrapper around legacy structure.\\012\\012#### C. Reference-only old surfaces\\012\\01210. Treat `_old` files as evidence/reference only.\\01211. Inspect them only when:\\012\\012* mechanic behavior is ambiguous\\012* edge-case expectations are unclear\\012* you need to avoid accidental mechanic drift\\012* you need to confirm that a presentation change will not break a real gameplay expectation\\012\\012#### D. Component-by-component verification during rewrite\\012\\01212. For each rewritten component or mechanic-facing subsystem, compare it against the old reference before finalizing.\\012\\012This includes, where relevant:\\012\\012* control/input behavior\\012* animation/update timing\\012* collision/contact behavior\\012* score/progress reporting\\012* fail/win transitions\\012* HUD feedback\\012* mobile tap/click paths\\012* gameplay-critical visibility\\012\\012If a rewritten component is more original but less stable, less testable, or mechanically less truthful, revise it.\\012\\012If a rewritten component is mechanically safe but visually generic, under-authored, or too similar to the old surface, strengthen the presentation before final handoff.\\012\\012### Rules\\012\\012* Do not let `_old` files remain the main implementation surface.\\012* Do not anchor the rebuild around editing `_old` files.\\012* Do not delete the old source.\\012* Do not rename remote/CDN URLs.\\012* Rename only directly linked local CSS/JS assets you can trace safely.\\012* Use blueprint and mechanic analysis as the first decision source; use `_old` files only as fallback clarification.\\012* Stability is more important than flashy technology choices.\\012* Originality matters, but not at the cost of breaking gameplay.\\012* Presentation should be meaningfully original when mechanic safety allows.\\012* Every major rebuilt subsystem should be explainable in terms of the blueprint and the old mechanic truth.\\012* Every major presentation subsystem should be explainable in terms of the remix premise, focal identity, and authored world.\\012* Do not name temporary original-game screenshot captures with `_old.png`; use `_trash.png` instead so they can be removed at the end of the run without confusing them with preserved `_old` runtime references.\\012\\012### Testing Plan Requirement\\012\\012You must follow a compact testing plan while rebuilding.\\012\\012At minimum, test:\\012\\012* boot/load success\\012* start/play flow\\012* active gameplay loop\\012* primary controls\\012* collision/hit behavior where relevant\\012* score/progress updates where relevant\\012* fail/win/restart behavior where relevant\\012* mobile-sized usability/readability\\012* HUD clarity and CTA reachability\\012* whether the transformed presentation still communicates the real objective\\012\\012Record what was checked and what still feels fragile.\\012\\012### Suggested Artifacts\\012\\012If feasible, write:\\012\\012* `clone_surface_map.json`\\012\\012  * old path\\012  * new `_old` path\\012  * role (`entry_html`, `css`, `js`)\\012  * reference-only flag\\012* `clone_rebuild_notes.md`\\012\\012  * what was preserved\\012  * what new public surface was created\\012  * where `_old` references were actually needed\\012  * what presentation surfaces were transformed\\012* `clone_rebuild_plan.md`\\012\\012  * blueprint/mechanics/reference interaction plan\\012  * fragile surfaces\\012  * easy-update surfaces\\012  * do-not-touch conceptual surfaces\\012  * focal identity and authored-world implementation plan\\012  * chosen engine/library approach and rationale\\012* `clone_rebuild_test_plan.md`\\012\\012  * what was tested\\012  * what passed\\012  * what remains risky\\012\\012### Success Condition\\012\\012This stage succeeds when:\\012\\012* Phase 1 has already defined the blueprint\\012* a pre-build plan exists describing how blueprint, mechanics, old references, and transformation surfaces interact\\012* the old runtime has been preserved under `_old` naming\\012* a new public `index.html` exists as the canonical surface\\012* the new game has begun as a blueprint-driven rebuild\\012* `_old` files are clearly demoted to reference-only status\\012* the rebuilt surface is stability-oriented, mechanically checked, and guided by an explicit testing plan\\012* the rebuilt surface is not merely the old game with themed paint\\012* the canonical surface has a clear path toward authored world ownership, focal identity, and mobile-readable presentation\\012\\012## Phase 3 — Authored World, Design-System, and Media
